page: Microsoft Azure EC4ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. The instance provides 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core using dedicated CPU allocation. Cache hierarchy features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a bundled 161 GB local SSD and zero dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate moderate single-thread execution alongside constrained multi-thread throughput. The single-core stress-ng score of 1986.87 and Geekbench single-core score of 1189.0 fall within the median range. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics remain modest due to the 4 vCPU topology, showing a multi-core stress-ng score of 3943.74, a Geekbench multi-core score of 2645.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 4713.07. Extended vector workloads lack AVX-512 and AMX extensions, while cryptographic workloads benefit from hardware acceleration instructions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, reflected in an average PassMark CPU encryption score of 2896.77.

The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio and bundled NVMe-grade SSD make the EC4ads_v5 cost-efficient for memory-centric and caching services rather than compute-bound operations. Evaluated against high-density compute tasks, performance is restricted by the limited core count, as seen in the PassMark database operations metric (1430.25) and Redis SET throughput (3.34 million operations/sec). The configuration functions effectively as an entry-tier host for in-memory caches, small-to-midsize relational databases, and intermediate data processing environments requiring high RAM density.
description: Microsoft Azure EC4ads_v5 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor, paired with 32.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per core) and 161 GB of local SSD storage. Designed with an x86_64 architecture and dedicated CPU allocation, it features hardware cryptography instructions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, but omits AVX-512 instruction sets. Benchmark performance shows median single-core output (Geekbench single-core of 1189.0, stress-ng of 1986.87) paired with modest multi-threaded throughput (PassMark CPU of 4713.07, Geekbench multi-core of 2645.0). Operating without GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, the instance offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio suited for workloads requiring elevated RAM allocations, such as in-memory caches, smaller relational databases, and light ETL tasks.
